title: Repeated phase transitions as a typed residency horizon
question: Across repeated semantic phase transitions, does FAULT_IN preserve its lower peak-memory advantage while accumulating materialization cost strongly enough to keep KEEP_WARM and FAULT_IN non-dominated on a typed frontier?
preregistered_gates: all high-quota runs complete without kernel OOM
job digests and per-transition workspace signatures match across residency modes and repetitions at each horizon
KEEP_WARM performs one capability materialization per worker while FAULT_IN performs one per worker per transition
FAULT_IN reduces measured kernel memory peak by at least 8 MiB at every horizon
KEEP_WARM has lower total materialization time at every horizon
both residency modes remain non-dominated on the two-objective memory-peak/materialization-time frontier at every horizon
long-horizon FAULT_IN total materialization time exceeds short-horizon FAULT_IN total materialization time
authority and retry authority remain unchanged
